```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

For the purpose of Bayesian species delimitation, with SNAPPER [@Stoltz2020], we need to
prepare the input file, which should be a Nexus file with SNP genotypes. Actually,
I advance that we have several options for generating a matrix of SNP genotypes,
and I think it's better to prepare more than one data set and run the same analysis
on all them, to check for robustness.

## Calling genotypes with ANGSD

At least, we have two sets of BAM files: those aligned to the reference genome in
`2023-05-18/BAM`, and those aligned to the set of ddRAD loci, in `2024-10-04/BAM`.

We already have selected variable sites with limited linkage disequilibrium and with
a minimum number of 60 samples with at least 2 reads covering the site. And we have
the genotype likelihoods of those sites in `../2024-03-11/Likes2/ARCTIC.beagle.gz`.
However, for some reason, ANGSD does not do the job when provided with the list of
sites and the genotype likelihoods. We have to feed it the raw BAM files and compute
the likelihoods all over again. I will filter later.

The method implemented by @Stoltz2020 is based on that of @Bryant2012, where the authors
explain very well how they compute the likelihoods. It turns out that the genotypes
are turned to allele frequencies. The model assumes a Fisher-Wright population mating
at random, but it does not model it explicitly. So, the important information in the
data is not the distribution of genotypes, but the allele frequencies. Actually, the
data file provided as an example suffers from a severe lack of heterozygotes. Thus,
it is not essential to get accurate genotypes. SNAPPER would probably work equally well on
haploids, or with a random sample of a single allele per site per individual. Thus, I
should not be worried about some heterozygotes being called homozygous when coverage
is low. I could use a low coverage threshold. But we do not need too many sites.

When calling genotypes another important argument is the posterior probability cutoff.
If the three possible genotypes were equally probable, the posteriors would be 0.33, and
a cutoff at that level would produce no missing data at all, but would introduce noise.
I am willing to confound a heterozygote for any of the homozygotes (with equal probability).
But I am not willing to confound the two homozygous genotypes. I will try with a cutoff
of 0.75, and see how much missing data we get.

Another consideration is whether to use only variable sites or also the
invariable ones. SNAPPER allows both. However, the interpretation of time units
when using only variable sites is unclear: perhaps, expected number of mutations
per site, knowing the site is variable? Such units are impossible to relate to
estimates of mutation rate. In addition, once we get the most *a posteriori*
probable genotypes, we may want to re-estimate nucleotide diversity measures,
which require invariable sites.

Yet, another consideration is Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. After having run the F$_{ST}$
analysis several times in folder `2024-10-10`, I realized several sites far from HWE
seem to be collapsed paralogy, and I think it's good to remove them. However, I am
not separating individuals by population or putative species when calling genotypes.
Thus, HWE does not apply.

```{bash}
SITES=../2024-03-11/Sites/ARCTIC_snp.sites
if [ ! -e GoodContigs.txt ]; then
   cut -f 1 $SITES | uniq | sed 's/$/:/' > GoodContigs.txt
fi

# Not excluding any individuals yet!
if [ ! -e bamlist1.txt ]; then
   ls -1 ../2023-05-18/BAM/*.bam > bamlist1.txt
fi
if [ ! -e toRef.geno ]; then
   if [ ! -e toRef.geno.gz ]; then
      angsd -bam bamlist1.txt \
            -ref ../2023-05-15/assembly.fasta \
            -out toRef \
            -baq 1 \
            -setMinDepthInd 4 \
            -minInd 80 \
            -GL 1 \
            -doMaf 2 \
            -doMajorMinor 1 \
            -doGeno 2 \
            -doPost 1 \
            -nThreads 8 \
            -postCutoff 0.75 1> toRef.log 2> toRef.err
   fi
   gunzip toRef.geno.gz
fi

if [ ! -e bamlist2.txt ]; then
   ls -1 ../2024-10-04/BAM/*.bam > bamlist2.txt
fi
if [ ! -e toRad.geno ]; then
   if [ ! -e toRad.geno.gz ]; then
      angsd -bam bamlist2.txt \
            -ref ../2024-10-03/consensus.fa \
            -out toRad \
            -baq 1 \
            -setMinDepthInd 4 \
            -minInd 80 \
            -GL 1 \
            -doMaf 2 \
            -doMajorMinor 1 \
            -doGeno 2 \
            -doPost 1 \
            -nThreads 8 \
            -postCutoff 0.75 1> toRad.log 2> toRad.err
   fi
   gunzip toRad.geno.gz
fi
```

## Filtering and preparing the input files for SNAPPER
### From alignments to reference

```{r}
toRef <- read.table('toRef.geno')
bams  <- scan('bamlist1.txt', what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)
samples <- sub('.bam', '', basename(bams))
rm(bams)
loci <- toRef[, 1:2]
names(loci) <- c('contig', 'pos')
geno <- toRef[, -c(1,2)]
names(geno) <- samples
plot(ecdf(colSums(geno >= 0)), xlab = 'Number of loci genotyped per sample',
     main = '', ylab = 'Cumulative fraction of samples')
abline(v = 200000, lty = 2, col = 'orange')
abline(v = 1000000, lty = 2, col = 'red')
```

I will include samples with at least 200000 genotyped loci, in order to
include the two individuals which seem to belong to a different
species, presumably *C. metoecus*, namely T165Cxa and S031Cmc. And for
the moment, I will keep only variable sites genotyped in these samples.

```{r}
MinLoci <- 200000
geno <- geno[, colSums(geno >= 0, na.rm = TRUE) > MinLoci]
rm(toRef, samples)
geno[geno == -1] <- NA
ObsHet <- sapply(1:dim(geno)[2],
                 function(x) {
                    sum(geno[, x] == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(! is.na(geno[, x]))
                 })
GeneticIds <- read.table('../2024-10-05/summary.txt', header = TRUE)
GeneticIds$species <- ifelse(GeneticIds$K2.1 > 0.95, 'pseudofarionis', NA)
GeneticIds$species <- ifelse(GeneticIds$K2.2 > 0.95, 'farionis', GeneticIds$species)
Species <- GeneticIds[match(colnames(geno), GeneticIds$Sample), 'species']
Species[is.na(Species)] <- 'unknown'
f1 <- Species == 'farionis'
f2 <- Species == 'pseudofarionis'
loci$freqFario  <- rowSums(geno[,f1], na.rm = TRUE) /
   (2 * rowSums(geno[, f1] >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
loci$freqFario <- ifelse(loci$freqFario <= 0.5, loci$freqFario, 1.0 - loci$freqFario)
loci$freqPseudo <- rowSums(geno[,f2], na.rm = TRUE) /
   (2 * rowSums(geno[, f2] >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
loci$freqPseudo <- ifelse(loci$freqPseudo <= 0.5, loci$freqPseudo, 1.0 - loci$freqPseudo)
loci$freqs <- rowSums(geno, na.rm = TRUE) / (2 * rowSums(! is.na(geno)))
par(mfrow = c(1,3))
barplot(table(round(loci$freqFario, 1)), las = 2, cex.names = 0.5, main = 'SFS C. farionis')
barplot(table(round(loci$freqPseudo, 1)), las = 2, cex.names = 0.5, main = 'SFS C. pseudofarionis')
boxplot(ObsHet ~ Species)

withMetoecus <- ! (is.na(geno[, 'S031Cmc']) | is.na(geno[, 'T165Cxa']))
geno <- geno[withMetoecus, ]
loci <- loci[withMetoecus, ]
Variable <- loci$freqFario + loci$freqPseudo > 0
genoVar <- geno[Variable, ]
lociVar <- loci[Variable, ]
```

I still need to remove positions in close linkage from others. The
strategy is to use the distances among adjacent loci. Such distances
are mostly short within a *locus*, and eventually larger among different
loci. Thus, I can assign a locus to every position and then select
one SNP (with highest MAF) per locus. I arbitrary set the distance
threshold to 1000, beyond which the SNPs are assigned different loci.
Of course, they are also different loci if they are in different contigs.

```{r, eval=TRUE}
library(plyr)
MaxDist <- 1000
numloci <- dim(genoVar)[1]
lociVar$dist <- c(NA, lociVar[2:numloci, 'pos'] - lociVar[1:(numloci-1), 'pos'])
lastcontig <- c('contig_null', lociVar[1:(numloci - 1), 'contig'])
lociVar[lociVar$contig != lastcontig, 'dist'] <- NA
rm(lastcontig, numloci)
lociVar$locus <- cumsum(is.na(lociVar$dist) | lociVar$dist > MaxDist)
lociVar$n <- rowSums(! is.na(genoVar))
selected <- ddply(lociVar, .(locus), function(x) x[which.max(x$freqs * x$n),])
selIndex <- match(paste(selected$contig, selected$pos, ":"),
                  paste(lociVar$contig, lociVar$pos, ":"))
selGeno <- geno[selIndex,]
GenoStrings <- sapply(selGeno,
                      function(x) {
                         x[is.na(x)] <- '-'
                         paste0(x, collapse = '')
                      })
write('#NEXUS',
      file = 'toRef.nex')
write('BEGIN Data;',
      file = 'toRef.nex', append = TRUE)
write(sprintf('\tDIMENSIONS NTAX=%i NCHAR=%i;',
              length(GenoStrings), nchar(GenoStrings[1])),
      file = 'toRef.nex', append = TRUE)
write('\tFormat datatype=integerdata symbols="012" missing=-;',
      file = 'toRef.nex', append = TRUE)
write('\tMatrix',
      file = 'toRef.nex', append = TRUE)
write.table(data.frame(Sample = names(geno), Genotypes = GenoStrings),
            'toRef.nex', quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = FALSE, append = TRUE)
write('\t;',
      file = 'toRef.nex', append = TRUE)
write('END;',
      file = 'toRef.nex', append = TRUE)
```

## Creation of a small data set for testing

I originally thought that a toy dataset should contain just far fewer
SNPs. Then, I learned that what actually reduces the speed of execution
of SNAPPER is the reduction of the number of individuals per species.
I will reduce both.

```{r, eval=TRUE}
toy <- selected[sample(1:dim(selected)[1], 1000),]
toyIndex <- match(paste(toy$contig, toy$pos, ":"),
                  paste(loci$contig, loci$pos, ":"))
hybrids  <- c('L019Cxa', 'L019Cxb', 'L088Cma', 'S023Cxd')
metoecus <- c('T165Cxa', 'S031Cmc')
farionis <- setdiff(grep('^L', colnames(geno), value = TRUE), c(hybrids, metoecus))
pseudofa <- setdiff(grep('^S', colnames(geno), value = TRUE), c(hybrids, metoecus))
few <- sort(c(hybrids, metoecus, sample(farionis, 10), sample(pseudofa, 10)))
toyGeno <- geno[toyIndex, few]
toyStrings <- sapply(toyGeno,
                      function(x) {
                         x[is.na(x)] <- '-'
                         paste0(x, collapse = '')
                      })
write('#NEXUS',
      file = 'toy.nex')
write('BEGIN Data;',
      file = 'toy.nex', append = TRUE)
write(sprintf('\tDIMENSIONS NTAX=%i NCHAR=%i;',
              length(toyStrings), nchar(toyStrings[1])),
      file = 'toy.nex', append = TRUE)
write('\tFormat datatype=integerdata symbols="012" missing=-;',
      file = 'toy.nex', append = TRUE)
write('\tMatrix',
      file = 'toy.nex', append = TRUE)
write.table(data.frame(Sample = few, Genotypes = toyStrings),
            'toy.nex', quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = FALSE, append = TRUE)
write('\t;',
      file = 'toy.nex', append = TRUE)
write('END;',
      file = 'toy.nex', append = TRUE)
```

## From alignments to ddRAD loci

```{r}
rm(list=ls())
toRad <- read.table('toRad.geno')
bams  <- scan('bamlist2.txt', what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)
samples <- sub('.bam', '', basename(bams))
rm(bams)
loci <- toRad[, 1:2]
names(loci) <- c('contig', 'pos')
geno <- toRad[, -c(1,2)]
names(geno) <- samples
plot(ecdf(colSums(geno >= 0)), xlab = 'Number of loci genotyped per sample',
     main = '', ylab = 'Cumulative fraction of samples')
abline(v = 500000, lty = 2, col = 'red')
```


```{r}
MinLoci <- 500000
geno <- geno[, colSums(geno >= 0) > MinLoci]
rm(toRad, samples)
geno[geno == -1] <- NA
ObsHet <- sapply(1:dim(geno)[2],
                 function(x) {
                    sum(geno[, x] == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(! is.na(geno[, x]))
                 })
GeneticIds <- read.table('../2024-10-05/summary.txt', header = TRUE)
Species <- GeneticIds[match(colnames(geno), GeneticIds$Sample), 'species']
Species[is.na(Species)] <- 'unknown'
f1 <- Species == 'farionis'
f2 <- Species == 'pseudofarionis'
loci$freqFario  <- rowSums(geno[,f1], na.rm = TRUE) /
   (2 * rowSums(geno[, f1] >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
loci$freqFario <- ifelse(loci$freqFario <= 0.5, loci$freqFario, 1.0 - loci$freqFario)
loci$freqPseudo <- rowSums(geno[,f2], na.rm = TRUE) /
   (2 * rowSums(geno[, f2] >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
loci$freqPseudo <- ifelse(loci$freqPseudo <= 0.5, loci$freqPseudo, 1.0 - loci$freqPseudo)

loci$freqs <- rowSums(geno, na.rm = TRUE) / (2 * rowSums(geno >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
loci$freqs <- ifelse(loci$freqs <= 0.5, loci$freqs, 1.0 - loci$freqs)
barplot(table(round(loci$freqs, 2)), las = 2, cex.names = 0.5, main = 'SFS')
loci$completeness <- rowSums(! is.na(geno))
plot(ecdf(loci$completeness), xlab = 'Samples genotyped',
     ylab = 'Cumulative fraction of loci', main = '')
```

I still need to remove positions in close linkage from others. The
strategy here is to keep only one SNP per ddRAD locus: the one that
maximizes the product of minor allele frequency and completeness.

```{r, eval=TRUE}
library(plyr)
MinCompleteness <- 80
MinFreq <- 0.25
#f <- loci$completeness >= MinCompleteness & loci$freqs >= MinFreq
f <- ! (is.na(geno[,'S031Cmc']) | is.na(geno[,'T165Cxa'])) & loci$freqs >= MinFreq
loci <- loci[f,]
geno <- geno[f,]

selected <- ddply(loci, .(contig), function(x) x[which.max(x$freqs * x$completeness),])
selIndex <- match(paste(selected$contig, selected$pos, ":"),
                  paste(loci$contig, loci$pos, ":"))
selGeno <- geno[selIndex,]
GenoStrings <- sapply(selGeno,
                      function(x) {
                         x[is.na(x)] <- '-'
                         paste0(x, collapse = '')
                      })
write('#NEXUS',
      file = 'toRad.nex')
write('BEGIN Data;',
      file = 'toRad.nex', append = TRUE)
write(sprintf('\tDIMENSIONS NTAX=%i NCHAR=%i;',
              length(GenoStrings), nchar(GenoStrings[1])),
      file = 'toRad.nex', append = TRUE)
write('\tFormat datatype=integerdata symbols="012" missing=-;',
      file = 'toRad.nex', append = TRUE)
write('\tMatrix',
      file = 'toRad.nex', append = TRUE)
write.table(data.frame(Sample = names(geno), Genotypes = GenoStrings),
            'toRad.nex', quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = FALSE, append = TRUE)
write('\t;',
      file = 'toRad.nex', append = TRUE)
write('END;',
      file = 'toRad.nex', append = TRUE)
```
